Thanks Anna — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments.

A couple of clarifying questions before procurement issues a provisional PO:
1) Line-item granularity: your catalog lists three SKUs but the billing team typically requires separate lines for subscription vs. premium support. Can you confirm which SKUs map to support add-ons?
2) Spend cap guidance: for a first-year estimate we typically set a provisional cap equal to the first invoice + 20%. Is $54k an acceptable provisional cap (covers $45k estimate + buffer)?
3) Billing entity: confirm the legal name and remit-to address for the PO.

Next steps: once you confirm the SKU split and remit address, I’ll loop in procurement (Marissa) to issue a provisional PO number and set a temporary spend hold until the DocuSign is executed.

Hi team —

I reviewed the attached catalog and vendor form. Procurement is prepared to issue a provisional PO; here's the decision and action list:

- Provisional PO number: PO-PROV-4782 (issued today).
- Provisional spend cap: $54,000 (per Anna's confirmation).
- Line-item corrections required: split the invoice into two accounting lines — 1) SKU-BAS-SUB (annual subscription) 2) SKU-BAS-SUPP (support credit). We will map SKU-BAS-INT to a separate prepaid pool if needed on subsequent invoices.
- Temporary restrictions: place a temporary credit hold on invoicing above the provisional cap until DocuSign for the Master Agreement is completed. This is standard practice for first invoices on new vendors.

Attachments: po_provisional_4782.pdf (provisional PO stub)

Please confirm that Anna's remit-to address is correct (copied below). Rishi — can you ask Anna to route the DocuSign to procurement@redwood.com and include the SOW ID (BA-4821-SOW1) in the subject so we can reconcile after signature?

Once the DocuSign is signed we will remove the temporary invoicing restriction and convert PO-PROV-4782 to the official PO number (or reissue if the final remit name changes).
